clue.text: Animated picture returned with wee statuette

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a GIF is a short looping animated image file

explanation.surface: A cartoon is made to go with a small statue, as if for a display.
explanation.walkthrough: "wee" looks like the Scottish word for small, sitting neatly beside statuette; here it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a figurine is a small modelled figure, the kind of ornament also called a statuette.

clue.text: Bold fellow starts to exercise in animal enclosure

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so exercise and in each give their first letter

parts.note: first letters of exercise and in

explanation.surface: A brave man starts working out inside an animal pen.
explanation.walkthrough: "in" looks like a link placing someone in the enclosure, but it supplies its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone feisty is spirited and ready for a fight, which is being bold.

clue.text: Cop following lead tips off local expert

parts.note: a cop books an offender, noting the charge

explanation.surface: A policeman chasing a lead passes information to someone who knows the area.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Cop a police officer; it is the verb, as in to book someone. A guidebook is a local expert in print form.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidebook gives the knowledge of a local expert about a place.

clue.text: Once again do up a derelict complex

indicators.note: intricate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renovate a run-down building block once more.
explanation.walkthrough: "do up" looks like a phrasal verb meaning renovate, but the definition ends at do and up joins the anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reduplicate is to repeat or double something, doing it once again.

clue.text: Place to jot down two potential answers to "A flat?"

parts.note: A flat is a musical note
a flat is also a pad, a place to live

explanation.surface: Somewhere to scribble your guesses for a crossword clue reading A flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives two answers to the same phrase: read as music, A flat is a NOTE; read as "a flat", a home, it is a PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper to jot notes down on.

clue.text: Expert professional solver cracks wordplay ahead of time

indicators.note: cracks means breaks into, so the solver goes inside the other letters
ahead of puts the wordplay first, in front of the time

parts.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay
a DI, Detective Inspector, is a police officer whose job is solving crimes

explanation.surface: A crossword pro solves the punning clues before the clock runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professional solver' looks like a crossword expert, but it is a detective, DI, who 'cracks' into PUN placed 'ahead of' T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an authority who gives opinions on a subject, especially in the media, so an expert.

clue.text: Method for extending life lapped up by Methuselah

indicators.note: held within, so the answer hides inside the word
in a down clue, read upwards, so the letters reverse

explanation.surface: The setter, named after the Bible's oldest man, drinks in the secret of long life.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is both the biblical man said to live 969 years and this setter's pseudonym. UHT milk is heat-treated to last for months, extending its shelf life.
explanation.definitionFit: UHT, ultra-high temperature treatment, extends the shelf life of milk.

clue.text: One serving queen or Medici, perhaps?

parts.note: the answer's pieces, a doctor and one, can be put back as medic and I, which run together as Medici; 'perhaps' flags the swap

explanation.surface: A courtier attending a Renaissance queen, perhaps one of the Medici family.
explanation.walkthrough: Medici suggests Catherine de' Medici, a queen of France, but split it as medic and I, a doctor and one; 'perhaps' warns the parts stand in for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee whose only role is to mate with the queen of the hive.

clue.text: Stray stayed with us several times a month

indicators.note: wander off course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, joined by with

explanation.surface: A stray animal lodged with us repeatedly each month.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stray" reads as a lost pet; it is the anagram signal. "with" simply joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Every month contains four or five Tuesdays, several times a month.

clue.text: Bloke taking drink which may scald tongue

explanation.surface: A man drinks tea hot enough to burn his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: "tongue" pairs naturally with scald as the body part; here it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue in its old sense of a language; Hebrew is the language of Israel and the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Revolutionary surrealist inspiring one urban myth

indicators.note: breathing in, so the reversed name takes I inside

parts.note: Salvador Dalí, the Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A radical surrealist artist sparks a city legend.
explanation.walkthrough: "urban myth" is a playful definition: the Iliad is a myth about a city, Troy, not a modern rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad tells the legend of the siege of the city of Troy.

clue.text: Age immediately following prohibition era in US

definitions.meaning: read as a historical period, the years just after Prohibition, and meant as a person's age, the one reached just after being barred from drinking
read as locating Prohibition in America, and meant as the country whose drinking age this is

explanation.surface: A historical note about what came straight after Prohibition in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The age read is historical, the years after 1933; the real sense is a person's age: the US drinking age is 21, reached right after the years when you are forbidden to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-one is the minimum legal drinking age in the United States.

clue.text: Repeat Phi puzzle in publication

indicators.note: as a verb, to confuse, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to run another of the setter Phi's puzzles in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is a fellow Independent setter, so the surface reads as a request to reprint one of his crosswords. The i is a British national newspaper, a sister title to the Independent.
explanation.definitionFit: The i paper is a British daily newspaper, a publication.

clue.text: Some illicit rendezvous get discussed online

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: News of a secret affair spreads across social media.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to trend is to be much talked about on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic trends when it is widely discussed online.

clue.text: Time machine transports rank little creatures with eight legs

parts.note: the Doctor's time machine in Doctor Who, the British TV series

explanation.surface: A time machine carries off some unpleasant tiny eight-legged animals.
explanation.walkthrough: "rank little creatures" reads as foul bugs; rank is the wordplay, meaning a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardigrades, or water bears, are microscopic animals with eight legs.

clue.text: Fellow like a certain piper is followed

parts.note: abbreviation for company fellow, as in co-worker
the Pied Piper of Hamelin, who led the rats and children away

explanation.surface: A man resembling the Pied Piper is trailed, as the children trailed him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper is famous for being followed, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have copied someone is to have imitated them, which is following their lead.

clue.text: Being this might make Spooner say "Bunk off? Whatever for?"

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was known for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to bunk off is British slang for skiving, to shirk

explanation.surface: An idle person, lazily mangled by Spooner, asks why they should bother skiving.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, shirk why with the SH and W sounds traded becomes work-shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone work-shy avoids labour, which is exactly what bunking off means, so the clue's spoken words describe the state.

clue.text: Argument on premises burst gym's lilos

indicators.note: broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A row on site after a gym's inflatable mattresses pop.
explanation.walkthrough: "on premises" looks like a place, on site; logically, premises are the statements an argument rests on. A lilo is an inflatable mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllogism is an argument drawing a conclusion from two premises.

clue.text: Arab king's flat guarded by a bit of muscle, I see

explanation.surface: A king's home is watched over by some muscle, as a bodyguard might say.
explanation.walkthrough: "flat" reads as the king's apartment; it means dull. King Abdullah has ruled Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdullah is the name of kings of Jordan and Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Pastry cook reduced hot liquid

explanation.surface: A pastry cook boils some hot liquid down, as in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pastry cook" reads as one job title, but the definition stops at Pastry and cook starts the wordplay; "reduced" sounds like a sauce but shortens BAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a sweet layered filo pastry with nuts and syrup.

clue.text: Texan city a famous Georgian proclaimed

indicators.note: announced out loud, so the answer is a sound-alike

parts.note: Jane Austen wrote in the Georgian era

explanation.surface: A city in Texas announced by a well-known person from Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgian suggests the US state next door in the surface; it is the British Georgian period, 1714 to 1830, when Jane Austen lived.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Austin is the state capital of Texas.

clue.text: Chill spike ultimately following low temperatures?

definitions.text: Chill spike ultimately following low temperatures?

indicators.note: following puts the last letters after the temperatures

parts.note: 1C twice: two readings of one degree Celsius, a low temperature

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A cold spike of ice forms when the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1C as IC: two such low temperatures give ICIC, and 'ultimately' takes the L and E ending chill and spike.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a chilly spike of ice that forms after freezing temperatures, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Writer's old love laying it on thick

parts.note: the writer is, I'm, from the setter's point of view

explanation.surface: An author's former sweetheart is flattering him far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: "laying it on thick" reads as heavy flattery; in painting it is literal, paint applied thickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying paint on thickly.

clue.text: Terribly exhausted locksmith declared "no rest for the wicked"

indicators.note: badly, so the letters are rearranged
emptied, so only the outer letters of locksmith stay

parts.note: locksmith with its middle emptied out
part of the letters to rearrange
part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A worn-out locksmith grumbles that the wicked never get a break.
explanation.walkthrough: "no rest for the wicked" is a proverb, but only rest for the wicked is the definition: a candle holder is a rest for something with a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle holder is where a wicked thing, a candle with a wick, rests.

clue.text: Couple finally dropping off obscure relative

indicators.note: two letters at the end are removed

parts.note: obscure as an adjective, hard to make out

explanation.surface: A pair nods off beside some distant relation.
explanation.walkthrough: "obscure relative" reads as a little-known family member; obscure is the wordplay and relative alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle, a parent's brother or an aunt's husband, is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Taxi driver getting the knowledge embracing one secretive group

parts.note: a learner driver, marked by an L-plate

explanation.surface: A London taxi driver studying the Knowledge joins a secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knowledge is the test of London streets a cabbie must pass, so the surface pictures a trainee cabbie; the wordplay just wants a learner, L. British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cabal is a small faction plotting together in private.

clue.text: Sellers of beauty products carrying uniform around explosive event

indicators.note: turned round, so the whole run reverses

parts.note: Avon representatives sell cosmetics door to door

explanation.surface: Cosmetics sales staff in uniform come to some dramatic event.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon is a cosmetics company whose representatives, Avon reps, sell door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a dying star blowing itself apart, among the most violent blasts in the universe.

clue.text: Sharing a tip, star signs books here

indicators.note: the two words share the A where one ends and the other begins, so it is written once

parts.note: Libra and Aries, two signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star autographs books in a shop while passing on a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: "star signs books" suggests a celebrity at a signing; here it is the zodiac. LIBRA ends and ARIES starts with A, the shared tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are places where books are kept, so books are here.

clue.text: Old president not quite retired

indicators.note: falling just short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: retired for the night, in bed

explanation.surface: A former president who has not fully stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: "retired" suggests leaving office; it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abe is the familiar short name of Abraham Lincoln, the 16th US president, long dead and so old.

clue.text: Such fruit passed round back of car

definitions.note: DRIED is an adjective; the definition works as "fruit that is dried".

indicators.note: the back of a car is its rear end, so the last letter of car is taken

explanation.surface: Some fruit is handed around in the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: "Such fruit" means the answer describes a kind of fruit, as in dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried fruit, like raisins and apricots, is a common kind.

clue.text: See 21
Dodgy come-ons landing male in hot water?

indicators.note: suspect, so the letters are rearranged
bringing in, as landing a fish

explanation.surface: Suspect flirting lands a man in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: "in hot water" means in trouble, but the definition is literal-ish: consommé is a clear soup, which looks like hot water. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear thin broth, which could jokingly pass for hot water.
